text:
Passive movements are movements of a body part produced by an external force—such as a therapist, machine, or gravity—rather than by the person's own muscle contraction. They are used in assessment (e.g., checking joint range of motion) and treatment (e.g., preventing stiffness when a patient cannot move actively). As the team note adds, they are performed without resistance and stop at the end of the available range rather than stretching beyond it.
CONFIDENCE: 95
